The hospital said there was no "active threat" within the hospital and patients and staff are safe.
"The campus is currently closed while law enforcement leads their investigation," the hospital said.

sources.news_title: Two officers shot inside Swedish Hospital on Chicago's North Side
sources.text:
1 Chicago police officer killed, another critical after shooting at Swedish Hospital on North Side
A Chicago police officer was killed and another officer is fighting for his life after they were shot inside Swedish Hospital in Chicago's Lincoln Square neighborhood on Saturday morning.
Law enforcement sources told CBS News Chicago the incident involved a prisoner in the hospital who managed to get hold of a gun and shot the two officers. The officers were taken to Illinois Masonic, where one was pronounced dead, and another was listed in critical condition.
The shooter then fled the hospital to a nearby home several blocks away. SWAT teams surrounded the home and later placed the shooting suspect in custody.
CPD Superintendent Larry Snelling, during a press conference, said the officer who died in the shooting was a 38-year-old and a 10-year veteran of the department. The second officer is 57 years old and a 21-year veteran.
Snelling said the suspect was originally taken into custody for suspected robbery. It is unclear why the suspect was taken to Swedish Hospital, but Snelling said it was for observation. He added that there was a third gun recovered, but it is unclear where the weapon came from.
The shooting prompted Alderperson Andre Vasquez earlier to ask residents to shelter in place.
Endeavor Health, in a statement, said, "No team members or patients were physically harmed as a result of this incident. The safety of our patients and team members remains our top priority. We are cooperating with law enforcement during their investigation and our deepest compassion remains with the officers and their families."
Investigation into the shooting remains ongoing.
This is a developing story. CBS News Chicago will continue to provide updates.

sources.news_title: Suspect in custody after 2 officers shot at Chicago hospital, police sources say
North Side hospital on lockdown after reports of shooter wounded officers
sources.text:
One Chicago police officer was killed and another critically injured after they were shot at Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital Saturday morning by a man they brought in for treatment at the emergency room, according to police and hospital officials. The suspect was taken into custody.
Chicago Police Superintendent Larry Snelling said in a department-wide message to police, obtained by the Tribune, that an officer assigned to the Albany Park (17th) District was shot and killed while transporting the suspect inside the Lincoln Square hospital. Another officer was also shot and remains in critical condition Saturday afternoon, he wrote.
Snelling called the shooting “a devastating loss for our department and our city” and called on the department to support the fallen officer’s family.
“This officer gave his life to protect his fellow Chicagoans, and we will never let our city forget his sacrifice,” he wrote.
The message did not name either officer.
Endeavor Health, which operates the hospital, said the suspected gunman was taken to the emergency department around 9 a.m. He fired shots at the officers about two hours later and escaped the building, at which point he was apprehended, officials said in a statement.
They also said the man was wanded when he arrived at the hospital per “public safety weapon detection protocols,” and that he was escorted by law enforcement at all times. No staff or patients were physically harmed during the shooting, the statement said.
“The safety of our patients and team members remains our top priority,” Endeavor Health said. “We are cooperating with law enforcement during their investigation and our deepest compassion remains with the officers and their families.”
Chicago police said more details would be released at a news briefing. At least one of the wounded officers was believed to have been rushed to Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center.
The Cook County medical examiner’s office, in a statement to the Tribune Saturday afternoon, said it had been notified of a death at the address of Swedish Hospital. The office did not share any further details.
According to a source familiar with the investigation, Albany Park (17th) district police originally arrested the suspect for an alleged robbery at a Family Dollar store in the 3200 block of West Lawrence Avenue shortly after 8 a.m.
A still from surveillance video footage obtained by the Tribune showed the suspect running naked down a street, with white patches stuck to his chest.
When the hospital went into lockdown amid reports of an active shooter around 11 a.m., emergency vehicles rushed down nearby streets and later lined Foster Avenue, which police blocked off from traffic near the hospital’s campus.
About a 10-minute walk east of Swedish Hospital, nearly half a block of houses on West Carmen Avenue were sectioned off with police tape Saturday afternoon.
Nicholas Brown, 29, who lives a couple of blocks away, watched the police search for the suspect. He said it seemed that police were searching for the suspect in yards, sometimes jumping over fences. He saw hundreds of officers in the area — some with assault rifles, police dogs and riot shields.
“I’ve lived here for a few years,” Brown said. “I’ve never seen anything like it.”
Jean Brown, who lives on West Carmen Avenue, said police apprehended the suspect from under the back deck of a house in the alley between her street and West Winona Street. Although she didn’t see the suspect, she said her neighbors spent the morning texting updates in a group chat. Those who saw the search unfold told her that they saw police take a naked man to a police car.
“It’s sad news from the hospital,” the 60-year-old said.
Around noon, Ald. Andre Vasquez, 40th, told residents in a community alert to shelter in place and avoid the area, saying that around 11:30 a.m., an incident occurred with “multiple shots fired and two officers shot, one in critical condition.”
Nearly an hour later, the alderman released another statement saying police confirmed a suspect had been placed in custody.
Tribune reporters Jeremy Gorner, Tess Kenny, Greg Royal Pratt and William Lee contributed to this report.

A suspect is in custody after two Chicago police officers were shot Saturday morning inside the Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital, killing one officer and leaving the other in critical condition, according to local reports.
The Context
The fatal shooting happened in the Lincoln Square neighborhood at around 10:45 a.m. local time.
Alderman Andre Vasquez of the 40th Ward posted on Facebook urging residents to shelter in place when the incident first happened, later confirming the suspect was in custody.
Vasquez urged people to stay away from the area, writing "there is an active situation currently at approximately 11:30 a.m. at Swedish Hospital and the 2600 block of W Winona with multiple shots fired and two officers shot, one in critical condition."
"Please shelter in place if you are in the surrounding area or avoid the area," he added. "Our office will send out a notification as soon as possible with information when available."
Newsweek reached out to Chicago Police and Chicago Fire by email Saturday for more information.
What To Know
Sources tell WGN‑TV the incident involved a prisoner who was at the hospital when gunfire erupted. Both officers were in critical condition, with one officer dying just hours later, according to NBC Chicago.
In a statement to Newsweek, the Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital wrote that "around 11:00am, there was a shooting," adding that "the campus is currently closed while law enforcement leads their investigation. We are not aware of any active threat within the hospital and patients and team members at Swedish Hospital are safe. "
In a follow-up statement, the hospital told Newsweek: "An individual in custody of law enforcement was brought in to Swedish Hospital Emergency Department for treatment at approximately 9:00 a.m. on Saturday April 25, 2026. In accordance with Endeavor Health public safety weapon detection protocols, this individual was wanded upon arrival. He was escorted by law enforcement at all times."
"The individual later fired shots at the law enforcement officers and exited the hospital building. He was apprehended and remains in custody," the statement continued. "No team members or patients were physically harmed as a result of this incident. The safety of our patients and team members remains our top priority. We are cooperating with law enforcement during their investigation and our deepest compassion remains with the officers and their families."

sources.news_title: Suspect In Custody After 2 Police Officers Shot At Swedish Hospital: Reports
sources.text:
LINCOLN SQUARE — A robbery suspect was recaptured after he fatally shot one Chicago Police officer and critically wounded another Saturday morning while the suspect was being treated at Swedish Hospital following his initial arrest, police said.
One of the officers, age 38, died following the shooting and the other, age 57, was critically wounded, said Chicago Police Superintendent Larry Snelling, in a news conference outside Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center, where the officers were taken for treatment. Snelling declined to release the deceased officer’s name.
The shooter was a patient brought into Swedish Hospital by law enforcement for treatment about 9 a.m. and the shooting happened about 11 a.m., according to a statement released on X.com by Endeavor Health. The person was searched for weapons — “wanded,” acording to the statement — as per the hospital’s protocol when they arrived.
The person was accompanied by law enforcement throughout his time at the hospital, but was able to fire shots and escape the hospital, according to the statement. The person was apprehended “and remains in custody.”
“We are cooperating with law enforcement during their investigation and our deepest compassion remains with the officers and their families,” Endeavor Health said.
One source told Block Club Chicago that an officer was transporting a patient at the hospital in the 2600 block of West Winona Street when the patient disarmed the officer and opened fire.
One officer was dead on the scene and another was critically injured, the source said. Two other sources also said one officer was dead.
A person believed to be the gunman was in custody by about 12:20 p.m. after a short manhunt, according to NBC5. Ald. Andre Vasquez (40th), whose ward includes the hospital, also said that a suspect was in custody.
Vasquez emailed neighbors to warn there had been an active shooter situation at the hospital, “with multiple shots fired and two officers shot, one in critical condition.”
Police on the scene confirmed that two officers were shot and taken to Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center, but had no further information about their conditions.
Vasquez warned neighbors to shelter in place and avoid the area around the hospital.
Police and SWAT team members could be seen around the hospital, which was on lockdown early in the afternoon.

An active shooter situation took place on Saturday at Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital in the Lincoln Square neighborhood of Chicago, leaving one police officer dead and another critically injured.
Alderman Andre Vasquez posted on social media that the "active situation" developed at around 11:30 am at Swedish Hospital and the 2600 block of W Winona, where multiple shots were fired and two officers were shot.
Police and SWAT teams were dispatched to the hospital on Saturday morning. According to WGN-TV, sources said the incident took place when officers were transporting a prisoner either to or from the hospital. A WGN-TV reporter also confirmed that an image circulating on social media of a naked man fleeing the scene is the suspect.
Following the incident, hospital officials released a statement:
“An individual in custody of law enforcement was brought in to Swedish Hospital Emergency Department for treatment at approximately 9:00a.m on Saturday April 25, 2026. In accordance with Endeavor Health public safety weapon detection protocols, this individual was wanded upon arrival. He was escorted by law enforcement at all times. The individual later fired shots at the law enforcement officers and exited the hospital building. He was apprehended and remains in custody. No team members or patients were physically harmed as a result of this incident. The safety of our patients and team members remains our top priority. We are cooperating with law enforcement during their investigation and our deepest compassion remains with the officers and their families.“
Law enforcement confirmed that the suspect was taken into custody around noon after a manhunt took place. One officer was pronounced dead, while the injured officer was taken to a local hospital in critical condition.
In a press conference on Saturday afternoon, Chicago police confirmed that officers transported a patient to the hospital at around 10:50 am for observation when they were shot. The deceased officer was 38 years old. Chicago police declined to release the names of the officers, citing privacy reasons for their families.

sources.text:
Chicago officer killed, another critically wounded in hospital shooting: police
CHICAGO - One Chicago police officer was killed and another critically wounded in a shooting at Swedish Hospital on the city’s North Side, authorities said.
What we know:
One Chicago police officer was killed and another critically wounded in a shooting at Swedish Hospital on the city’s North Side, authorities said.
What we know:
The shooting occurred about 10:50 a.m. Saturday after two Chicago police officers transported an individual to Swedish Hospital for observation, Chicago Police Superintendent Larry Snelling said.
Further details on what led up to the shooting are limited, but both officers were shot.
According to Snelling, one of the officers, 38, was critically wounded and later pronounced dead. The other officer is 57 years old and is hospitalized, in critical condition.
The 38-year-old officer was a 10-year veteran of the department and the other officer is a 21-year veteran of the department. The identities of the officers haven't been released.
Authorities said a suspect is in custody and a weapon was recovered. The investigation is ongoing.
A spokesperson for Endeavor Health, which runs the hospital, said the hospital campus was closed due to the shooting.
They added the hospital was "not aware of any active threat within the hospital" and that patients and staff are safe.
We'll bring more updates to this story as they become available.

sources.news_title: Suspect in custody after shooting at Chicago hospital leaves 1 police officer dead, 1 in critical
sources.text:
Editor's note: Chicago police are expected to provide an update at around 4 p.m. Watch live in the player above.
A suspect is in custody after a shooting inside a Chicago hospital left one police officer dead and another critically injured on Saturday morning, law enforcement sources said.
Stream NBC 5 for free, 24/7, wherever you are.
Around 10:45 a.m., two Chicago police officers were shot at Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital, located at 5140 N. California Ave. in Chicago's Ravenswood neighborhood.
Police took the suspect to the hospital to be checked out before going to jail for a separate offense before the shooting broke out, police sources told NBC Chicago.
One of the officers was shot in the head, sources told NBC Chicago. Both were taken to a different area hospital, where one was later pronounced dead and the other was initially listed in critical condition.
A manhunt for the suspect ensued, with authorities swarming the hospital and the nearby area. Alderman Andre Vasquez asked residents in the surrounding area to shelter in place amid the manhunt.
The suspect was taken into custody around noon, authorities said.
Local
Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital was placed on lockdown after the shooting. The lockdown was lifted by 2 p.m., but the hospital remained closed.
Endeavor Health said the suspect was brought in for treatment around 9 a.m. and was scanned for weapons upon arrival, in accordance with the hospital's public safety weapon detection protocols.
The suspect was "escorted by law enforcement at all times" while in the hospital before escaping after the shooting, Endeavor said in a statement around 1:30 p.m. "No team members or patients were physically harmed as a result of this incident. The safety of our patients and team members remains our top priority."
"This is a horrible situation all around. Hoping the staff and those present at Swedish Covenant Hospital are also okay," said Alderman Gilbert Villegas in a post on social media.
Police blocked the streets surrounding the hospital as authorities investigated.
"Like everybody out here, we want to know what's happening, we want to find out," Ald. Vasquez said at the scene. "But we also want to make sure we're giving all the associated parties, the officers, the hospital, anyone out here now, the liberty and latitude to do the work that's necessary to make sure folks walk away safely from what has occurred and that we get the information necessary to make sure justice is served and we have information on what may need to be improved as far as protocol."
Handfuls of neighbors came outside to see what was going on as officers flocked to the area.
Vavid Stevens, a resident who lives on the block of the hospital, said he heard "a bunch of commotion going on" and looked out his window to see "more and more police cruisers coming by" his house.
Then, his mom called him, he said. She told him to come outside because she'd "never seen anything like" what was going on.
Stevens said his mom described to him seeing police officers with guns drawn---a sight he said people are not used to seeing in his "quiet" neighborhood.
"It's horrible to know that something like this happened," Steven said. "It's a very grim situation."
Steven said his mom also expressed concern and fear knowing the suspect ran into the neighborhood and officers were hunting for him with guns drawn.
"There's countless officers out here at the scene, so that speaks volumes to what happened," another neighbor said. "I mean, they're everywhere."
Several CTA buses were rerouted due to police activity in the area.
As of 1 p.m., #92 Foster buses and #93 California/Dodge buses were rerouted in both directions due to the ongoing investigation.
"Allow extra travel time," CTA said on its website.
Garfield Ridge Neighborhood Watch will host a prayer vigil for the officer who was killed at 6 p.m. at Hale Park, located at 6258 W. 62nd St., the group said in a post on social media.
"All are welcome to join," Garfield Ridge Neighborhood Watch said in the post.
No additional information was immediately available.
Check back for more on this developing story.

sources.news_title: Chicago hospital goes on lockdown after shooting that reportedly injures two officers
sources.text:
CHICAGO — A shooting at a Chicago hospital Saturday morning is under investigation.
Endeavor Health Swedish Hospital said a shooting happened at the facility around 11 a.m. Central Time, prompting the campus to go on lockdown while police investigated the area.
Hospital officials said they were not aware of any active threat within the hospital shortly after noon local time and said patients and team members at the hospital were safe.
Several elected officials provided details about the incident and urged people to stay away from the area during the investigation.
Alderman Jim Gardiner said two officers were reportedly shot during the incident.
According to Alderman Andre Vasquez, the suspected shooter was in custody shortly after noon local time. Vasquez also said one of the officers was in critical condition.
Alderman Gilbert Villegas thanked public safety officials for their "quick response and swift action."
"Sending my thoughts and prayers for a quick recovery for the officers injured," Villegas wrote on X. "This is a horrible situation all around. Hoping the staff and those present at Swedish Covenant Hospital are also okay."
This story is developing and will be updated as information becomes available.
